title: Regional maintenance caused SLO erosion due to circuit-breaker templating bug and uneven standby eviction
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a scheduled control-plane maintenance on 2026-02-12 we observed an unexpected SLO erosion in region eu-west-1 and spillover latencies in us-east-1. The failure mode combined (1) a templating bug that caused non-uniform circuit-breaker thresholds to be applied to rolling pools, (2) an aggressive standby eviction during maintenance that produced uneven capacity, and (3) delayed alerting because SLO evaluation was using global aggregated windows rather than per-region windows. This ticket contains the incident timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations applied during the event, and follow-up action items with owners and due dates.
timeline:
2026-02-12T02:00Z: Start of scheduled control-plane maintenance for config push to eu-west-1.
2026-02-12T02:07Z: KPIs show rising p99 latency in eu-west-1 from 220ms baseline to 540ms.
2026-02-12T02:09Z: Traffic routed to secondary regions as expected, us-east-1 tail latency climbs to 780ms.
2026-02-12T02:12Z: Automated circuit-breaker triggers in eu-west-1 for some pools; due to templating bug thresholds applied were 3x lower for one pool (pool-A) compared to others.
2026-02-12T02:15Z: Standby eviction job (maintenance script) aggressively reclaimed cold standby nodes in eu-west-1 to drain for patch; capacity dropped 18%.
2026-02-12T02:20Z: Prefix/KV cache warmup failures observed for rerouted traffic; cache miss rate spiked 6x.
2026-02-12T02:28Z: Aggregated SLO alert fired (global window) instead of per-region alert; on-call routed to follow-up triage.
2026-02-12T02:40Z: Emergency rollback of templated config push and rollback of standby eviction mitigations.
2026-02-12T03:10Z: Latencies return to baseline; monitoring shows gradual KV cache warmup over next 90 minutes.
root_cause:
1) Templating bug: a legacy templating script used to build circuit-breaker configs had a conditional that mis-read regional tags during a zero-downtime config push. For one pool (pool-A) in eu-west-1 the cb.threshold and cb.min-concurrency values were lower than intended (threshold 30 -> 10). This caused premature tripping and amplified reroute fanout.
2) Standby eviction sequencing: a maintenance script intended to cordon and drain nodes evicted standby nodes before graceful scaling of active shards, lowering capacity headroom by ~18%.
3) Monitoring/alerting granularity: SLO evaluation and alerting were configured primarily on aggregated account-level percentiles, obscuring regional regressions until amplification occurred.
4) KV cache cold-start sensitivity: rerouted requests relied on warmed KV caches; the sudden fanout and cache misses increased per-token CPU and tail latencies.
detection: Initial detection via p99 latency dashboards in the runtime console (on-call noticed p99 > 500ms in eu-west-1). However, the principal SLO alert was global and thresholded to a 60-minute window; it did not escalate quickly. Synthetic regional probes were present but muted during maintenance windows. The first human escalation arrived at 02:14Z following dashboard anomalies and customer complaints via support channel.
mitigation_summary: Immediate actions taken during event: 1) Rolled back control-plane config push to restore correct templated cb values (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/7842). 2) Temporarily disabled aggressive standby eviction script and re-provisioned 3 standby nodes to restore headroom. 3) Applied temporary region-specific circuit-breaker overrides to add buffering capacity while KV caches warmed (playbook step CB-E-OVERRIDE-1). 4) Escalated to oncall-sre and opened priority incident bridge. Post-event measures included a targeted smoke-test and KV cache rewarm job.
action_items: A1: Fix templating script to validate region tags and thresholds; add unit + integration tests for template outputs. Owner: Priya Nair. Due: 2026-02-26. LINK: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RI/CB+Templating+Fix

A2: Change maintenance standby-eviction sequencing to cordon -> scale-up replacement -> drain -> evict. Owner: Marco Hernandez. Due: 2026-03-01. Deliverable: updated maintenance runbook and automation patch (infra repo PR).
A3: Implement per-region SLO evaluation windows and dedicated region alerts (short window for rapid detection). Owner: SRE team (lead: Omar Kim). Due: 2026-02-23. Metric ticket: ENG-100101

A4: Add a canary validation step to config-rolls that asserts circuit-breaker configs against a governance policy (min/max thresholds per pool). Owner: Platform Config Team (lead: Elena Rossi). Due: 2026-03-05. Policy stored at: /policy/cb-thresholds.md

A5: Improve KV cache warmup by adding proactive rewarm for expected rerouted traffic patterns and allow transient increased token-burst budget during maintenance. Owner: Runtime Team (lead: Kenji Sato). Due: 2026-03-10.

A6: Update alerts so synthetic probes are not muted during controlled maintenance windows or create a separated maintenance probe with guardrails. Owner: Observability (lead: Maya Li). Due: 2026-02-20.
A7: Run chaos test that simulates partial regional capacity reductions during releases and validate failover stability and SLO impact. Owner: Resilience Eng (lead: Diego Alvarez). Due: 2026-03-20.
A8: Postmortem review with the oncall rotation rotation and revise runbook to include a 'rapid rollback' path for templated config pushes. Owner: Incident Commander (Aisha Patel). Due: 2026-02-19.
